==English== ===Pronunciation=== * {{IPA|en|/sɛl/}} * {{audio|en|en-us-sell.ogg|a=US}} * {{homophones|en|cel|cell|;|sail|sale|Sal}} * {{rhymes|en|ɛl|s=1}} ===Etymology 1=== {{root|en|ine-pro|*selh₁-}} From {{inh|en|enm|sellen}}, from {{inh|en|ang|sellan||give; give up for money}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*salljan}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*saljaną}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*selh₁-}}. {{col-top|2|cog}} Cognate with {{cog|sco|sell|t=to sell}}, {{cog|da|sælge|t=to sell}}, {{cog|nb|selge|t=to sell}}, {{cog|nn|selja}}, {{m|nn|selje|t=to sell}}, {{cog|sv|sälja|t=to sell}}, {{cog|fo,is|selja||t=to sell}}, {{cog|got|𐍃𐌰𐌻𐌾𐌰𐌽|t=to pay tribute, make an offer}}. {{col-bottom}} ====Verb==== {{en-verb|~s|~ing|sold}} # {{senseid|en|peddle, vend, supply in exchange for money}} {{lb|en|transitive|ditransitive|intransitive}} To transfer [[good]]s or provide [[service]]s in [[exchange]] for [[money]]. #: {{syn|en|peddle|vend|Thesaurus:sell}} #: {{ant|en|buy|purchase|Thesaurus:buy}} #: {{ux|en|She '''sold''' her old car very quickly.}} #: {{ux|en|I'll '''sell''' you three books for a hundred dollars.}} #: {{ux|en|Sorry, I'm not prepared to '''sell'''.}} #* {{RQ:KJV|Matthew|19|21|passage=If thou wilt be perfect, go and '''sell''' that thou hast, and give to the poor.}} #* {{RQ:Economist|date=2013-08-10|volume=408|issue=8848 |title=[http://www.economist.com/news/leaders/21583270-new-zealands-plan-regulate-designer-drugs-better-trying-ban-them-and-failing-new A new prescription] |passage=No sooner has a [synthetic] drug been blacklisted than chemists adjust their recipe and start churning out a subtly different one. These “legal highs” are '''sold''' for the few months it takes the authorities to identify and ban them, and then the cycle begins again.}} # {{lb|en|ergative}} To be sold. #: {{ux|en|This old stock will never '''sell'''.}} #: {{ux|en|The corn '''sold''' for a good price.}} # {{senseid|en|promote (a product or service) although without pay}} {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[promote]] (a product or service) although not being paid in any direct way or at all. #* {{quote-av|en|year=2016|chapter=The Fetal Kick Catalyst|title=w:The Big Bang Theory |passage=Howard: You're gonna feel terrible when I'm in a wheelchair. Which, by the way, would fit easily in the back of this award-winning minivan.
Bernadette: Fine, we'll go to the E.R. Just stop '''selling''' me on the van.
Howard: You're right. It '''sells''' itself.}} # {{senseid|en|promote (a viewpoint)}} {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[promote]] (a particular viewpoint). #: {{ux|en|My boss is very old-fashioned and I'm having a lot of trouble '''selling''' the idea of working at home occasionally.}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[betray]] for [[money]] or other things. #: {{syn|en|sell the pass|sell down the river|sell out|Thesaurus:betray}} # {{lb|en|transitive|slang}} To [[trick]], [[cheat]], or [[manipulate]] someone. #* {{RQ:Jonson Volpone|passage=Then weaues
Other crosse-plots
New tricks for safety, are sought;
They thriue: When, bold,
Each tempt's th'other againe, and all are '''sold'''.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1884|author=w:Mark Twain|title={{wsource|The Adventures of Huckleberry Finn}}|chapter=XXIII |passage=House was jammed again that night, and we '''sold''' this crowd the same way.}} #* {{quote-journal|en|date=January 12, 2011|author=Saj Chowdhury|work=BBC |title=[http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/9345343.stm Blackpool 2-1 Liverpool] |passage=Raul Meireles was the victim of the home side's hustling on this occasion giving the ball away to the impressive David Vaughan who slipped in Taylor-Fletcher. The striker '''sold''' Daniel Agger with the best dummy of the night before placing his shot past keeper Pepe Reina.}} # {{lb|en|transitive|professional wrestling|slang}} To pretend that an opponent's blows or maneuvers are causing legitimate injury; to act. # {{lb|en|slang|intransitive}} To [[throw under the bus]]; to [[let down]] one's own [[team]] in an [[endeavour]], especially in a [[sport]] or a [[game]]. #: {{ux|en|He's '''selling'''!}} #: {{ux|en|He really '''sold''' in that match.}} =====Antonyms===== * {{l|en|buy}} =====Derived terms===== It'll be an awful '''sell''' if at the end you have to acknowledge you've [[make a hash of|made a hash of]] it."}} #* '''1922''', {{w|Katherine Mansfield}}, ''The Doll's House'' (Selected Stories, Oxford World's Classics paperback 2002, 354) =====Derived terms===== {{col2|en|soft sell|hard sell|tough sell|sell-up}} ====See also==== * {{l|en|sale}} ===Etymology 2=== From {{bor|en|fr|selle}}, from {{der|en|la|sella}}. ====Alternative forms==== * {{alter|en|selle||obsolete}} ====Noun==== {{en-noun}} # {{lb|en|obsolete}} A [[seat]] or [[stool]]. #* {{RQ:Tasso Fairfax Godfrey of Bulloigne|book=4|stanza=7|page=56|passage=The tyrant proud frown’d from his loftie '''cell''', [...].}} # {{lb|en|archaic}} A [[saddle]]. #* {{RQ:Spenser Faerie Queene|passage=turning to that place, in which whyleare / He left his loftie steed with golden '''sell''', / And goodly gorgeous barbes, him found not theare [...].|2|2}} ===Etymology 3=== From Old Saxon [[seill]] or Old Norse [[seil]]. Cognate with {{cog|nl|zeel||rope}}, {{cog|de|Seil||rope}}. ====Noun==== {{en-noun}} # {{lb|en|regional|obsolete}} A [[rope]] (usually for tying up cattle, but can also mean any sort of rope). #: {{ux|en|He picked up the '''sell''' from the straw-strewn barn-floor, snelly sneaked up behind her and sleekly slung it around her swire while scryingː "dee, dee ye fooking quhoreǃ".}} =====Derived terms===== * [[bowsell]] ====References==== * [http://www.dsl.ac.uk/entry/snd/sell_n1 The Dictionary of the Scots Language] ===Anagrams=== * {{anagrams|en|a=ells|ELLs|Ells|ells}} {{cln|en|calculator words|irregular verbs}} {{C|en|Business|Money|Prostitution}}
